newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Delta sets gold output record in Mch qtr.
newsitem.headline: Delta sets gold output record in Mch qtr.

text.p: Delta Gold NL said on Tuesday that it achieved record quarterly gold production and its lowest cash production cost in nearly seven years in the March quarter.
Production totalled 69,812 ounces, up from 46,214 ounces in the December quarter. The previous company record was 50,308 ounces in the March quarter of 1996.
The average cash cost per ounce was A$224, the lowest achieved since June 1990, the company said.
Chairman Jim Vanderspuy said the rise in production was largely due to record production of 120,992 ounces from the 40 percent owned Granny Smith mine in Western Australia.
"Granny Smith continues to outperform expectations and is a great asset for Delta," Vanderspuy said in a statement accompanying the company's quarterly report.
He said Granny Smith production for the quarter, 41,822 ounces more than the previous quarterly record in March 1996, was achieved on exceptionally low cash costs of A$202 per ounce.
The other 60 percent of Granny Smith is owned by Placer Pacific Ltd, a unit of Placer Dome Inc.
Vanderspuy said the Granny Smith operation was well on its way to eclipsing the record of 284,616 ounces of gold produced in the 1995/96 year ended June 30.
The Kanowna Belle mine, owned 50 percent by Delta, contributed production of 42,832 ounces and is on track to produce 170,000 ounces for the financial year, Vanderspuy said.
Kanowna Bell, owned 50 percent by North Ltd, produced 152,832 ounces in the year to June 1996.
"For gold deliveries during the quarter, Delta exceeded the spot price by A$66 an ounce, realising A$518 per ounce compared with the average spot price of A$452," the company said.
